title: Rep. Burgess Owens highlights military family support and transit funding for Utah - West SLC News
text:
Rep. Burgess Owens, who represents Utah’s 4th District in the U.S. Congress, shared updates on recent legislative efforts and funding developments through a series of posts on December 2, 2025.
In a post at 21:23 UTC, Owens expressed support for legislation aimed at helping military families. He stated, “Military families in Utah’s Fourth District and across the country sacrifice so much for our nation and we owe them a debt of gratitude. Proud to support @RepRichHudson’s Love Lives On Act to ensure the surviving spouses of our fallen servicemembers don’t lose their benefits if”.
Later that evening at 22:34 UTC, Owens announced significant federal funding for local transit modernization efforts. He wrote, “Great news for Utah riders: @USDOT has awarded more than $41 million to modernize transit across the Fourth District.
$21.33M for clean-diesel bus replacements at @RideUTA
$20.47M for new low-emission CNG buses
This funding helps @RideUTA modernize its fleet and improve”.
At 23:19 UTC, Owens addressed air travel disruptions attributed to a government shutdown and highlighted his involvement with aviation-related legislation. He posted, “The Democrat Shutdown caused chaos at airports nationwide, from air traffic control shortages to stranded passengers. I co-sponsored @RepAaronBean’s Aviation Funding Stability Act to make sure the FAA stays operational during a lapse in government funding, keeping safety programs”.
Burgess Owens has represented Utah’s 4th District since replacing Ben McAdams in 2021. Born in Columbus, Ohio in 1951, Owens resides in Salt Lake City and holds a Bachelor of Science from the University of Miami (FACTS 1-4).
